title: Syntagma sacrae theologiae (Liber I Cap. 3 densify)
author: Ludwig Crocius
edition: Syntagma sacrae theologiae (Bremen: Berthold Villerian, 1636). VD17 14:684303C. SLUB id335860389. Liber I Cap. 3 De sacra Scriptura (complete through II; Cap. 4 starts PHYS 177).
blurb: Ludwig Crocius — Book I Chapter 3 On Sacred Scripture from the 1636 Bremen Latin. Complete Cap. 3 densify: written revelation as first analytic principle called Sacred Scripture; analytic ministry not magisterium; against mixing philosophy into the articles of faith; the Word of God as rule of faith; whatever Scripture teaches is infallibly true, against the papal first principle, circularity, with Bereans, Moses, Prophets, Christ, and Apostles; analogy with naturally known principles and Scripture's spiritual efficacy, through the bridge to affections and parts. Cap. 4 begins PHYS 177; the rest of the Syntagma remains.
era_note: Crocius wrote in the early seventeenth century as Reformed professor at the illustrious school of Bremen. This is not a patristic work. It is a public-domain Latin Reformed retrieval on the same Fathers-site pipeline. The 1636 Villerian folio is Public Domain Mark 1.0. Do not treat the site as ante-Nicene only.
first_english_note: No complete public-domain English of this 1636 Latin Syntagma was locked as reading text. This is a new rendering from locked Latin for Liber I Cap. 3 complete.

text_history.method: English follows the locked 1636 Bremen Latin of Liber I Cap. 3 complete (I-II), reconstructed from SLUB Dresden page images (PHYS 169-176). Same-page OCR (tesseract lat + Vision) used as check. No modern English was copied. Cap. 4 (CAPUT QUARTUM) begins PHYS 177. No Internet Archive copy was located.
